h: Getting the best out of a Dreamland day
p: Dreamland is easy to reach without a car. Margate railway station is only a short walk from the park and the beach, so the train is a stress-free way to arrive, especially on busy summer days when parking along the seafront fills up fast.

How long to allow depends on your crew. Ride-loving kids and teens can happily make a full afternoon of it, going back for second goes on their favourites, while a family with toddlers might be ready for a sit-down after a couple of hours. Have a look at ride height guidance before you go, so nobody gets their heart set on a coaster they can't go on yet.

The Scenic Railway is the one everyone wants to say they've ridden. It's a proper piece of seaside history, and part of the joy is the clatter and rattle that modern coasters simply don't have. Even if you're not riding, it's a cracking thing to watch.

Once you're done, Margate has plenty to fill the rest of the day. The Shell Grotto, an underground passage lined with millions of shells whose origins are still a bit of a mystery, is one of the town's real curiosities. The Harbour Arm is a nice stroll for sea views and a bite to eat, and Broadstairs, with its pretty bay and old-school ice cream parlours, is just along the coast if you fancy a change of scenery.
Gig nights bring a very different crowd and atmosphere, so if you're visiting with little ones, a non-event day is usually the calmer choice.
